farming._doc: DENOMINATION (T3.2b/CR-002): yieldPerArableKm2PerYear is food units per FERTILITY-WEIGHTED km2 per year, against CatchmentSummaryRow.EffectiveArableKm2. One food unit = one person-year of adult-equivalent sustenance, so the constant reads directly as the person-years of food an ideal-suitability (f=1.0) km2 yields per year. It is a CAPACITY (what a saturated territory can produce), not an observed density. It replaces yieldPerFarmlandPerYear = 28.0, which was denominated per fertility-weighted lattice NODE (256 km2) and therefore implied 0.109 person-years/km2 = ~9 km2 of land per person; at a 2.5% sown share that is a sown yield of 8.8 kg/ha against a sowing rate of 120-200 kg/ha, i.e. it did not return the seed by a factor of ~700. See docs/adr/cr-002.md for the derivation.
farming._docValue: DERIVED, NOT FITTED (T3.2b item 1); full chain, sensitivity and cross-checks in docs/adr/adr-013. Four independent reference-class derivations plus three adversarial attacks (fitting / units / labour-interaction), all three refuted; the synthesis re-derived the REFERENCE CLASS from the sim's own worldgen rather than picking one off the shelf, which is what settled it. Worldgen step 6 defines fertility = clamp(tempSuit x moisture x 1.6-if-river-adjacent, 0, 1) with moisture = 1/(1 + d_water_px/40) and 4 km pixels, so f = 1.0 is attainable ONLY within 8 km of a river channel and at mean annual temperature in [8.4, 23.6] C. The sim's ideal square kilometre is therefore RIVER-VALLEY FLOOR AND FIRST TERRACE in a temperate-to-warm climate - well-watered valley bottom, not average upland - and every land-use share must be a share of THAT landscape. CHAIN: 770 kg/ha long-run mean sown yield (frequency-weighted, valley bottom); minus 120 kg/ha broadcast seed (seed:yield 6.4:1, inside the 5-10:1 rainfed band); x0.90 storage and threshing loss = 585 kg edible per sown ha; cropped share of the territory at saturation k = 0.28 (deducting channel/floodplain 12, slope and terrace break 15, pasture for the traction and manure herd 25, woodland 15, settlement 5 ha per 100); medium fallow, crop 2 years in 7 = 0.2857, so 8.00 sown ha per f=1.0 km2; 4,680 kg edible; / 180 kg clean grain per adult-year (2,200 kcal/day, cereals 75% of calories, 3,390 kcal/kg) = 26.0. INVERSE CHECK: 0.88 arable ha per average person, against Wilkinson's and Halstead's 0.5-1.0 for pre-mechanised rainfed - inside, mid-range. SENSITIVITY: k alone 16.7-37.1; fallow alone 14.0-45.5; all endpoints simultaneously 5.5-133.8. THE WORLD IS OUT OF CORRIDOR AT THIS VALUE - see docs/adr/cr-003.md, which escalates it rather than absorbing it by moving a band. NOTE THE DENOMINATION: 26.0 is per fertility-weighted km2. The per-NODE equivalent 26.0 x 256 = 6,656 belongs only to the retired yieldPerFarmlandPerYear; writing it here would be exactly the 256x fault CR-002 closed.

preCultivation._doc: R2a (Director decision 8: 'Do not fabricate an agricultural yield while claiming Agriculture is unavailable'). ISOLATED CONTENT SWITCH: when enabled, a settlement whose knowledge does not make activity.farming eligible (research.json sectorActivities, mode replaces) harvests WILD FOOD at these rates; the CR-003 cultivated 26.0 / 5.0 apply once farming is known. Values FIXED BEFORE MEASUREMENT (CR-003 5.1), reference class = ethnographic forager carrying capacity. yieldPerArableKm2PerYear DERIVED 1.0 person-years per fertility-weighted km2: food unit = one person-year, so a forager population at carrying capacity has density = yield. Binford (2001, Constructing Frames of Reference) and Kelly (2013, The Lifeways of Hunting and Gathering Peoples) put the median forager density near 0.1-0.2 persons/km2, with the richest riverine/acorn-salmon foragers (California, Northwest Coast; Kroeber 1939) at 0.5-2 per km2. The sim's f=1.0 km2 is river-valley floor in a temperate-to-warm climate (see farming._docValue), the richest class, so the log-midpoint of 0.5-2 = 1.0 (26x below the cultivated 26.0). outputPerGathererPerYear DERIVED 2.0 person-years per gathering adult per year: Kelly (2013) - a forager producer supports about 1.7-2 consumers (vs the cultivated 5.0). enabled: the orchestrator's switch (see the R2a report for the measured calibration consequence). R4 RE-CALIBRATION (Director 2026-10-04: raising primitive gathering yield is the preferred lever; agriculture stays researched; smallest defensible value, not a maximum; sweep in docs/r4a-m5-closure-record.md). MEASURED: the R2a values 1.0 / 2.0 starve the founding world (the labour side binds: per gatherer x the 0.55 never-ordered food-sector share x the adult share is below consumption at any population). outputPerGathererPerYear 4.3 is the smallest value on the measured grid at which the dev worlds starve nobody: per FOOD-SECTOR worker 4.3 = 2.37 person-years per ADULT once spread over all adults (0.55 x 4.3), inside the forager producer range Kelly (2013) and Kaplan et al. (2000, Evolutionary Anthropology 9:156) report - a prime-age forager producing about 1.7-3x own consumption; the R2a 2.0 applied Kelly's per-producer ratio to the 55% food-sector share only. 4.25 starves 5 people on dev seed 7. yieldPerArableKm2PerYear 2.0: the TOP of the R2a reference range (richest riverine foragers 0.5-2 per km2); 1.0 and 1.5 let the dev worlds hit the forager land ceiling and starve hundreds. Agriculture (cultivated 26.0 / 5.0) still raises the land ceiling 13x and per-worker output by 16%.

catchment._doc: The ECONOMIC HINTERLAND radius (T3.2b): the country whose produce can profitably flow to the settlement, NOT a farmer's daily working radius. Stated as an IDEAL-GROUND radius in km and converted to the pathfinder's cost budget by LatticeGeometry.CostUnitsForIdealGroundKm; what it actually buys is decided by geography - shorter through mountain and marsh, longer along rivers and built dirt paths, which is how a road network grows a hinterland (D-009). Replaces the code constant CatchmentSystem.TravelBudget = 15.0 cost units (= 240 km ideal ground, ~205 km measured), which no tuning pass could see and which was compensating for the yield denomination error.
catchment._docSizeBonus: T3.8 catchment bonus. sizeBonusMaxRatio: CHOSEN 0.10 within a stated frame - a fully built-out settlement extends its effective hinterland by at most a tenth (second-order vs geography; 0.5 would let size dominate terrain, 0.01 would be decorative). sizeDwellingsRef: DERIVED 70 = founding-scale dwelling demand (~410 founding pop / 6 persons per dwelling), so a founding settlement sits near the top tier and the bonus SATURATES rather than compounding with growth. Quantized to five tiers so the D-016 recompute gate survives (a continuous dwellings budget would re-run the partition Dijkstra every turn).

transport._doc: T4.7 (THE TRANSPORT PACKET). riverCostFactor 0.20: the cost of moving ALONG a river as a fraction of IDEAL GROUND (movement cost 1.0), i.e. the r of T3.6b's water counterfactual. REFERENCE CLASS, stated at T3.6b BEFORE any number was computed: pre-modern freight-cost ratios (Diocletian's Price Edict, corroborated by medieval English cartage-vs-river rates) put ROAD : RIVER per ton-km at roughly 5-10 : 1, giving the ratified band r in [0.10, 0.20]. 0.20 is the CONSERVATIVE edge of that band - the 5:1 end, the WEAKEST river advantage the reference class supports - chosen because it is also the edge with a MEASURED outcome: T3.6b's pixel-resolution counterfactual at r = 0.20 produced 4/27 ore-trade-pair crossings against 0/27 on the river-blind lattice. Picking the strong edge (0.10) would have manufactured a larger effect from the same evidence. CARRIER: a coefficient inside TraversalLattice.Build's per-block cost aggregation - nodeCost = (1-span)*blockMeanCost + span*riverCostFactor, span = min(1, riverCells/stride) - so a river that fully threads a stride block prices that block at exactly r, which is what the pixel counterfactual charges for the same crossing. NOT a second graph, NOT a NetworkEdge, NOT persisted state: TerrainSet remains the authoritative geometry (ADR-008 - derived terrain is neither serialized nor cloned). Rivers do NOT change passability; river cells are LAND. Vessels, ports and naval movement are OUT OF SCOPE.

consumption._docStoreBounding: T4.2 (B-2 BASE LAYER). Two DERIVED constants, reference classes stated in docs/t4.2-manifest.md and fixed BEFORE the world was run. grainSpoilagePerYear 0.08: threshed cereal in pre-modern FIXED storage (mud-brick or pit granary, no chemical protection, no controlled atmosphere) loses 5-10%/yr to moulds, germination, insects and rodents; the midpoint is taken, not tuned. Carrier: decay. granaryYearsOfDemand 1.5: an agrarian household carried on the order of one to a few years of its own consumption; the midpoint is taken. Carrier: a structure of finite size, which grows with the settlement because more households means more granaries. NOT A CAP CHOSEN TO MAKE FAMINE APPEAR (CR-003 5.1): spoilage ALONE equilibrates at 12.5 years of surplus (0.08*S = s), which is why B-2a stages two layers - the capacity ceiling is what binds, and that was derived and stated in the manifest before measuring.
consumption._docEmpireFoodAllocation: INTRA-POLITY GRAIN RELIEF IN A SHORTAGE. Authority: D-053 section 2 (docs/d053-batch2-playtest-rulings.md, the Director's 2026-10-13 instruction, item 2: food allocation in a shortage); D-053 section 5 records that it supersedes D-052 section 11's 'no partial pooling / no relief-pooling substitute' for this item. It is a PARTIAL step toward D-051 section 6's ratified direction (one central stockpile per civilization, food included), NOT that stockpile: every store, its spoilage and its granary bound stay per settlement, and grain moves only in a shortage, only inside one polity. empireFoodAllocation true: after every settlement has eaten from its own store, a settlement a polity controls whose GRAIN ROW IS EMPTY and whose nutritional requirement is still unmet is a claimant; every settlement of that polity whose grain row still holds grain is a donor (so a settlement one unit short BESIDE a stocked granary - the floating-point remainder edge - stays a donor, never a claimant). Donors' grain is moved to claimants instantly and losslessly, BEFORE spoilage and the granary bound are applied per settlement exactly as before. A settlement no polity controls is its own store. WHO IS FED FIRST - IDENTITY, no coefficient: max-min water-filling on the NOMINAL DEFICIT (the unmet fraction of each claimant's nutritional requirement, the recorded deficit ratio, which is the INPUT to FoodState's effective deficit). Within one food state this ranks exactly by starvation risk; across food states it does not (a FAMINE-class settlement at deficit 0.25 has effective deficit 0.25, a NORMAL or SEVERE one at 0.30 has 0.125), because the food state the demographic kernel applies is classified from tables other systems write in the same step. Whole-unit leftovers by (unmet fraction, previous turn's food state - a one-turn-lagged tie-break only, settlement id). WHERE IT IS DRAWN FROM - IDENTITY: nearest donor first, ties by id (ADR-032, the order roads already pay in). No new demographic or mortality rule: the deficit ratio keeps its meaning and counts the food received. false or absent = the per-settlement store, byte for byte (the attribution control, TestConfigs.PreEmpireFoodAllocation).

demographics._docHeadroomRelaxation: T4.21 (ADR-025 2.4 / ADR-026; docs/t4.21-architecture.md 3.5c, 3.6b). headroomRelaxationPerYear (k): the per-year rate at which a settlement's REMAINING food headroom (N_lim - N, Sim.Core/State/FoodHeadroom.cs) is closed by natural growth (the Demographics headroom cap, T4.21-3) AND by immigration (Migration's vacancy bound, T4.21-2): cap = (1 - exp(-k*dt)) * V. ONE law, ONE constant, consumed by both systems. TUNE, CHOSEN per S8 4.1(c) - not derived: k = ln 2 / 10 = 0.0693147180559945 within the director's frame 'the gap halves per decade' ((1 - e^{-k*h}) = 3.41% of remaining headroom per half-year). No null arm by design - a structural bound has no switch (law 2); the identity arm is N_lim = +inf (no deficit row / no demand), where the cap is vacuous. Adding the key (T4.21-1b) changes no behaviour until its consumers ship; the goldens do not move.

founding._docCohortCounts: T4.19 lane C (director ruling on the T4.18 diagnosis, docs/m4-population-transient-investigation.md; record: docs/m4-founding-demographics-correction.md). The previous vector [46,44,40,30,28,26,24,22,20,18,17,15,30,20,12,8] put 70/400 = 17.5% of the founding population in cohorts 12-15 (ages 60-79), where mortalityPerYear runs 0.107-0.305/yr, so the shipped world opened by losing 22% of its people in three turns (seed 42: 5,140 -> 4,330 -> 4,041 -> 3,987) to births-minus-deaths alone - an initialization artefact, not a mechanism. This vector is the MEASURED stable age structure of the shipped fertility/mortality/aging kernel, not a derivation on paper: DemographicsSystem run ALONE (pipeline ['demographics'], deficit 0, dt 10) from the old vector x1000 converges in cohort SHARES by turn 8 to [0.1432 0.1399 0.1271 0.1134 0.0992 0.0853 0.0721 0.0597 0.0482 0.0376 0.0280 0.0198 0.0129 0.0074 0.0037 0.0023] - identical at turns 50/100/200/400, identical at dt 5, identical from a uniform start - and settles at +0.0761 %/yr (CBR 4.172, CDR 4.096 per 100/yr). Those shares apportioned to the SAME total of 400 by largest-remainder rounding (lowest-index tie-break) give this vector; Sim.Tests FoundingDemographicsTests re-derives it from the kernel on every run and pins the equality, so the number cannot drift from its derivation silently. 60+ share is 11/400 = 2.75% against the kernel's 2.63%. NOT CHANGED: foodStore (the food endowment scales with REALISED population, so founding food per capita is unchanged to the unit - measured per settlement, seed 42), endowmentJitter, and every demographic rate. NO startup modifier of any kind exists; the world simply starts on the age structure its own rates support.
founding._docEndowmentJitter: T3.6b (ADR-017): 0.25 -> 0.69, DERIVED - the RC-1 reference-band FLOOR, the smallest intervention the Item 0 measurement justifies. RC-1 (committed before the measurement was seen, docs/t3.6b-spec.md): Neolithic settlement-size distributions and village-fission founder groups justify founding-population CV 0.4-0.6; the uniform u in [-1,1] jitter realises CV = amplitude/sqrt(3), so the band floor CV 0.4 gives amplitude 0.4*sqrt(3) = 0.6928 ~ 0.69 (measured at 0.25: CV 0.115-0.161 across five seeds, below the band). The T3.1c structure is unchanged: food scales with REALISED population (only the amp/3 per-capita wobble is independent), so founding food-per-capita stays stable and the measured colony-crash mode stays closed. NOT justified by trade and may never be re-tuned against a trade observable (CR-003 5.1; the pre-committed P2 reading predicts trade unchanged by this value). ADR-035 s7 (2026-10-07): this amplitude now drives the settlement-COMMON factor only; the per-cohort factor is demographic-scale noise, amplitude min(1, sqrt(3/n_c)) for a cohort of expected count n_c (CV ~ 1/sqrt(n_c), the multinomial founder-group reference class).

migration._docDamping: T3.2b RENAME ONLY, value unchanged. Lattice cost units — the same units as SettlementDistanceRow.TravelCost, which is correct here: this damps travel EFFORT, not map distance. 25 cost units is ~400 km across ideal ground and materially less across hard country, which is the intended behaviour.
migration._docLandWeight: T4.10 (director ruling, Option A): the PAIRED attractivenessFoodWeight was REMOVED and the attractiveness food term with it, so the balance described below no longer has two sides - R is now LandWeight x arableKm2 alone. T4.2 bounded the grain store (spoilage + granary capacity), which destroyed raw stock as an attractiveness signal: an adequately-fed and a moderately food-short settlement both converge toward near-zero post-consumption stock. The replacement signal considered (1 - DeficitRatio) measured IDENTICALLY 1.0 across the canonical world (4 seeds x 3 checkpoints x 12 settlements, DeficitRatio exactly 0 everywhere), contributing zero differential, so no coefficient for it was derivable, validatable or refutable. Food now reaches migration only through famineFlightFactor and destinationDeficitRepulsion. NOTE for whoever re-derives landWeight (T4.12 owns that): landWeight CANCELS EXACTLY from the m* gap-closing cap once food is gone, so it now scales the attractiveness GAP only, not the cap. The historical two-term derivation is preserved below for provenance. --- T3.4b RE-DERIVATION (CR-003 2.6). NOT a rescale to reproduce old behaviour - the old balance was a product of the wrong denomination and has no claim to correctness. DERIVED FROM WHAT THE SIGNAL SHOULD DO, measured in the weather-live dev world at turn 120: food/capita runs 1526-1544 across settlements (a 1.2% spread, roughly 5000 years of stores - the pre-Malthusian frontier CR-003 describes), while arable/capita runs 0.162-4.698 (a 26x spread). Migration responds to the GAP in attractiveness, not its level, so at the previous weights food supplied ~20x the differential land did while being nearly uniform: the land signal was effectively dead and migration was reading noise on a saturated stock. STATED POSITION: in a frontier world the driver of movement is LAND OPPORTUNITY, because everyone is fed and only room to farm distinguishes one site from another; when land fills and stores thin, HUNGER must take over as the driver. The weights are therefore set so the two terms contribute COMPARABLY to the differential at FED conditions - which makes hunger automatically dominate the moment food actually varies, since famine moves food/capita by orders of magnitude while land's spread stays 26x. The driver SWITCHES WITH THE REGIME rather than being hardwired, which is the emergence property CR-003 requires. Land differential at fed conditions: (4.698-0.162)*0.078125 = 0.354, against a food differential of ~0.35. 0.078125 = 5/64 exactly, so the weight stays a clean binary fraction and the product remains exactly representable.
migration._docHappinessWeight: T4.13 (director ruling): happiness is a WEAK migration input; food and material survival stay dominant. CHOSEN 0.15 within a stated frame, not derived - there is no measurement that could derive it, because happiness is new and no historical series contains it, and inventing a derivation would be a false provenance claim. The frame: happiness must be able to break a TIE between two materially similar destinations without being able to override a material difference. Land attractiveness across the canonical world spreads ~26x (see _docLandWeight); a modulation of 0.15 moves viability by at most 15%, which is far inside that spread and therefore cannot reorder two destinations whose land differs materially, while it does reorder destinations whose land is comparable. The mechanism is multiplicative on VIABILITY, so it composes with - and never bypasses - the deficit repulsion and the absolute food gate: a famine-struck or foodless destination is still viability 0 whatever its happiness, which is the ruling's requirement that severe famine not be cured by migration. Raising this toward 1.0 continuously strengthens happiness as a driver; 0 disables the input entirely and recovers exactly the pre-T4.13 behaviour, which is the arm the tests use to prove the term is doing the work.

classes.name: Artisans
classes._doc: Artisans emerge on TWO necessary conditions (T3.1): food_surplus_ratio - the food exists to feed a non-farmer - AND population - a market exists to buy from him. The second is Smith's extent-of-the-market limit on the division of labour (Wealth of Nations I.iii); it is also the registry's only SCALE-DEPENDENT term, so founding-size variation reaches the crossing time through it (see Sim.Core/State/Variables.cs). TUNE: 520 sits above the ~350-500 jittered founding sizes, so every settlement must GROW into its artisans.

classes.name: Merchants
classes._doc: T4.11. Merchants emerge on OBSERVED TRADE VOLUME - the whole units that actually moved through the settlement last turn (Sim.Core/State/Variables.cs, trade_volume) - and on the same extent-of-the-market population term artisans use. A merchant lives by moving goods between places, so the gate is the movement itself rather than a proxy for it: where the arbitrage deadband never opens, volume is zero and no merchant ever appears, which is the honest outcome for a world whose settlements have nothing to gain by exchanging. TUNE, stated as CHOSEN within a MEASURED frame rather than derived, because no historical series contains this variable. Measured on the canonical world (seed 42, 12 settlements) per-settlement volume is EPISODIC, not smooth: max 114 at turn 100, 135 at 200, 2 at 300, 227 at 400, 3042 at 650, with only 2-4 settlements carrying any flow at a time - the deadband opens and closes as prices drift, so the signal spikes. 200 sits above the early-world chatter and inside the range the maturing world reaches repeatedly; the recede floor of 50 is deliberately far below it, because what turns this spiky signal into a durable class is the D-020 HYSTERESIS LATCH - a settlement that crosses once stays a merchant town until trade genuinely dries up, which is what the latch is for and why a single threshold would have oscillated on and off. EXTENSION SEAM: long-distance shipping, foreign trade and multiple cargo classes all add movement this same variable sums, so richer logistics arrive as a larger numerator and never as a replacement for the merchant identity.

mobility._doc: T3.3 DEMOLITION: toolYieldBonusCap/Slope and constructionLaborWeight DELETED (m3 spec 1, mandated). Tools are a real good consumed by farmers (see production); sector labor pools are class-blind shares of the adult workforce (D-032).

production._doc: T3.3 (D-032). ALL CHOSEN, not derived - stated per S8 4.1(c); each value's real-world meaning and plausibility frame is in ProductionConfig's doc. outputPerHerderPerYear: food units per herder-year at deposit 1.0 (3.0 - below the farmer's 5.0, above self-subsistence 1.0). outputPerExtractorPerYear: raw-good units per extractor-year at deposit 1.0 (4.0 - sized against recipe input demands). toolsPerFarmerToEquip: 1.0 (one man, one tool set). toolYieldBonusMax: labor-side factor 1 + bonus x equipRatio at full equipment (0.3 - magnitude carried from the retired scaffold cap; mechanism new: real stock per farmer, not a class share). toolWearPerEquippedFarmerPerYear: 0.1 (a tool set lasts ~10 working years).

price._doc: T3.4 price solver (D-033). ALL TUNE, ALL CHOSEN - not one value derived, stated explicitly per S8 4.1(c); each value's real-world meaning and plausibility frame is in PriceConfig's doc. lambda: price-adjustment speed per sim-year (0.04 - a 100% sustained relative excess moves price 4% per year, ~25-year e-folding. SIZED AGAINST THE COARSEST SHIPPED dt: the Neolithic band steps 10 sim-years at once, so lambda*dt must stay well under 1 or a single turn overshoots the equilibrium it is seeking. An earlier 0.35 gave lambda*dt = 3.5 and drove prices to opposite ends of the band at dt=10 vs dt=1 - caught by the dt-invariance test, not by inspection). marketScaleFloorPerYear: divide-by-zero guard with a meaning - the reference size below which a market is too thin for relative excess to mean anything (0.1 units/year). PER YEAR and integrated with dt: it sits in the denominator of excess/scale whose numerator scales with dt, so a dt-independent constant made the ratio dt-DEPENDENT exactly where the floor binds - the one place the system's dimensionless claim was false, found by the T3.4 dt-determinism lens. 0.1/yr reproduces the previous 1.0 exactly at dt=10. stockReleaseRatePerYear: fraction of a held stock offered to market per year (0.5 - half the granary comes to market, the rest is seed corn and insurance; this is the term that lets a full warehouse damp a spike). bandMin/bandMax: hard bound on any price in grain units (0.05 / 20.0 - deliberately WIDE; the band's job is to stop divergence, not to express economics, and a price resting on an edge means the band is doing work it should not be). maxRelativeChangePerYear: the per-step rail (0.03 - a price may not move more than 3% of itself per sim-year, i.e. 30% in a 10-year Neolithic turn and 3% in a 1-year turn. Sized so the rail BINDS at the coarsest dt rather than being decorative there: at the earlier 0.5 the rail permitted a 500% move in a single dt=10 turn, which is not a rail. Also keeps the step positivity-preserving without help from the band - a maximum downward move of 0.3p can never reach zero).

housing._doc: T3.8 (director ruling: maintenance, not abstract decay). Provenance per S8 4.1(c); reference classes committed in docs/t3.8-spec.md BEFORE measurement; the CLAY ARM CORRECTED at the certification fix pass (docs/t3.8-review-record.md, fix pass Item 1) - see the clay note below. tauYears: DERIVED 40 (band 25-60) - zero-maintenance habitable life of a neolithic dwelling (LBK timber-post rebuild cycles ~25-50y, mudbrick 50-100 with continual replastering); the e-fold of unmaintained decay, so one 10-year turn without upkeep loses ~22% of stock. upkeepTimberPerDwellingYear: DERIVED 0.05 = timber build cost / tauYears (2.5%/yr, band 2-5% - rethatch every 2-5y, member replacement). upkeepClayPerDwellingYear: 0.0 - CORRECTED DERIVATION. The original 0.025 drew on the registry good 'clay', which is the SELECTED RIVERINE CERAMIC MATERIAL (depositChannel water, the pottery input). Dwelling maintenance's earthen component - daub replastering, mudbrick repair - uses locally dug subsoil tempered with straw and dung (borrow pits beside the houses are a standard excavated feature of LBK and Near Eastern settlements), a UBIQUITOUS material that never passed through the potter's selected-and-levigated clay stream. Structural earth is therefore a non-good, like water: present, not modeled, not drawn. The original derivation checked the timber arm against shipped production but named the wrong registry good for the earthen arm - the measured consequence (housing's Leontief starved by pottery's input draw from turn 1) is recorded in the review record's after-column. buildTimberPerDwelling: 2.0 - the frame; scale checked against shipped production (~70 dwellings for a founding settlement = 140 timber vs measured ~24/yr output: a build-out takes years, not turns). buildClayPerDwelling: 0.0 - CORRECTED with the upkeep arm, same reasoning: earth walls are built from on-site subsoil, not the ceramic clay stream. The MIX statement becomes: timber frame + earthen walls-from-subsoil, with timber the only DRAWN material. personsPerDwelling: DERIVED 6 (band 5-8). buildLaborAdultYearsPerDwelling: CHOSEN 0.5 within a stated frame (a household raises a house in a season with help). surplusCapRatio: CHOSEN 1.2, mechanism shape - houses are built for households, not stockpiled; the cap stops construction labor compounding into a dwelling mountain while allowing a vacancy margin.

trade._doc: T3.6 trade & arbitrage (D-034). Provenance per S8 4.1(c), stated per value. gapClosingFraction: CHOSEN 0.25, never derived - the TUNE fraction f of the gap-closing quantity a connected pair moves per turn; the mandate fixes only f < 1 (structural no-overshoot: flow is a damped step toward price parity, never past it - the migration gapClosingFraction shape, T2.8) and the loader REFUSES anything outside (0,1). costPerBulkCostUnit: DERIVED 0.16 grain-value units per (bulkPerUnit x travel-cost unit) - the conversion that puts transport cost in the same unit as a price gap. Anchor: carting grain roughly doubles its cost within ~100 km overland (the same reference-class result the bulk table is reviewed against); grain has bulk 1.0 and price = 1.0, so ~1.0 grain-value per 100 km; one travel cost unit = 16 km ideal ground (kmPerPx 4.0 x lattice stride 4), so 100 km = 6.25 cost units and 1.0/(1.0 x 6.25) = 0.16. Rough terrain costs more per km than ideal, which points the right way: mountain routes trade less, river/path routes more.
trade._docEntity: R2a (Director decision 1): trade BETWEEN settlements (domestic or foreign arbitrage) is a research unlock. A pair trades only when the Trade capability - this research entity, knowledge-eligible through the settlement's knowledge (SettlementKnowledge: controller's knowledge, or a city-state's own) - holds at BOTH endpoints. Within-settlement consumption is not trade and is never gated.

harvestVariance._doc: T3.4b harvest variance (CR-003 ruling 3). ALL TUNE, ALL CHOSEN - none derived, stated per S8 4.1(c); full model and plausibility frames in HarvestVarianceConfig's doc. Log-space AR(1) per settlement with a spatially smoothed innovation; the multiplier is mean EXACTLY 1 (the -sigma^2/2 correction), so weather changes the VARIANCE of yield and never its expectation - which is what keeps the derived 26.0 a statement about land quality under normal conditions. sigmaLogYield: SD of LOG yield in one year, DERIVED (0.2936). Reference class: rain-fed cereal agriculture without irrigation or modern inputs, for which the best-documented proxy is medieval English demesne wheat (Winchester Pipe Rolls, 13th-15th c.), interannual yield CV commonly placed around 0.25-0.35. Early agriculture should sit at least that high: landrace seed, no systematic rotation, and - specific to this model - a ~50 km hinterland is a spatially small sample with little internal averaging. Taking CV = 0.30 as the central value and inverting the lognormal relation CV = sqrt(exp(sigma^2)-1) gives sigma = sqrt(ln(1+CV^2)) = 0.2936. The previous 0.18 was CHOSEN and implied CV = 0.18, below the whole reference band. correlationTimeYears: e-folding memory (3.0 - THE parameter that makes MULTI-YEAR DROUGHTS possible, which the ruling requires: consecutive failures are what kill, against stores that survive one bad year). spatialSharedFraction: share of the innovation coming from the regional field rather than a local draw (0.6 - the ruling requires this be meaningful, because uncorrelated rolls let trade and migration average all risk away and regional bad years are the point). spatialRangeCostUnits: e-folding distance of the weather field in IDEAL-GROUND travel-cost units applied to the GEOGRAPHIC straight-line distance between settlement sites (km / km-per-cost-unit; M5 R2b: weather does not follow roads, so road-aware SettlementDistances are not read) (40.0 - a weather system spans a region, not a continent). timeAveragedHarvest (D-051 ruling 1(b), 2026-10-10): true = a turn's harvest multiplier is the TIME-AVERAGE of the yearly weather process over the turn's max(1, round(dt)) yearly sub-steps (mean unchanged; per-decade log-spread ~0.30 -> ~0.19) and a new settlement joins the process at a stationary draw; false = the pre-1(b) single point draw per turn, bit-exact, which exists ONLY as the golden-attribution control (TestConfigs.PreTimeAveragedHarvest) - never a gameplay setting.

foodState._doc: T4.21-1 (CR-015 3.1/3.2, FAMINE IS EXCEPTIONAL). adaptationAbsorbableShortfall (a): CHOSEN 0.20, TUNE, with a stated physiological frame. ONE boundary carries the kernel semantics: a is BOTH the dead-zone of the effective deficit (d_eff = 0 for d <= a; (d - a)/(1 - a) above, exactly 1 at d = 1 - starvation mortality's one input outside FAMINE) AND the SEVERE threshold (theta_sev := a), so the state label predicts the kernel's response: STRESS (0 < d <= a) => no starvation; SEVERE (d > a) => starvation on the unabsorbed remainder; FAMINE (d > 0 with an applied disaster or deliberate abandonment) => starvation on the whole deficit. Frame: sustained ration cuts of ~15-25% are survivable without excess mortality (WWII civilian rationing; the Minnesota Starvation Experiment's ~50% cut for 24 weeks with no deaths is the upper bound), while 40-70% cuts (Dutch Hunger Winter, post-war German rations) carried excess mortality - the band's midpoint taken. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE a = 1/3: aligns the dead zone with the demographic kernel's birth full-stop at d = 1/famineFertilitySuppressionSlope (births continue exactly while nobody starves); not the default because the director's own frame puts survivable cuts at 15-25%. NULL ARM a = 0 reproduces the pre-T4.21 linear response bit for bit. Every OTHER reader of the deficit (fertility suppression, the rebound release gate, destination viability, happiness, appropriation, demote-first) keeps the NOMINAL d. Loader refuses values outside [0,1).

disaster._doc: T4.21-1 (CR-015 3.3): the explicit FAMINE-CLASS production shock - one kind (crop failure), multiplying the same two FOOD paths harvest weather multiplies (farming + herding/fishing), never extraction, never stores, never reading population or deficits (like weather it cannot decide famine; FoodState does, from the balance). ALL TUNE. hazardPerYear (lambda): DERIVED AT 0.01, SHIPPED AT 0.0 - THE MECHANISM IS COMPLETE AND TESTED BUT INERT, AND THE RATE IS THE DIRECTOR'S TO RULE. The sequence, truthfully: T4.21-1 SHIPPED IT AT 0.0 (the plumbing packet - its golden move is layout + RngStreams only); T4.21-4 ARMED IT AT THE DERIVED 0.01 - one famine-class local crop failure per settlement per century - and MEASURED the fallout (CR-001's PERMANENT dt-continuity detonator broken across the turn-250 dt 10 -> 5 gate by 2.2572 per 1000 yr on the battery rig (seed 1, windows 1600-2500/2500-3400: +0.4352 -> -1.8220) and 2.5259 per 1000 yr on the DemographyRetuneTests rig (+0.7616 -> -1.7643), against a 0.1 bar on both - see CR-016 D.6, the two are DIFFERENT RIGS and 2.1's table combines them; canonical.fedGrowthPerYear 0.000407442 below its immovable band [0.0005, 0.001]; canonical turn-300 population at a median 0.26 of the unarmed world; the dev world extinguished 93,910 -> 38 over 1000 turns), and escalated it rather than absorbing it; CR-016 (OPEN - docs/adr/cr-016-armed-disaster-fallout.md) RETURNS IT TO 0.0 pending the director's ruling, because choosing a lower rate that made the world survive would be tuning-to-outcome, which CR-015 6.5 forbids, and the honest act is to decline to ship an unvalidated calibration rather than invent a validated-looking one. THIS NUMBER IS THE ONLY THING UNSET: the mechanism is proven by the forced-strike rigs, the ladder tests and the determinism legs, so it is ONE DATA EDIT (0.0 -> 0.01, or whatever the director rules) away from live. The derivation, the reference class and the BAND below are UNCHANGED - they are not what CR-016 disputes. Reference class: pre-modern European regional famines - England 1300-1700 ~5-6 famine-class events / 400 y (~1/70 y); France by region 1500-1800 (Le Roy Ladurie) 1/50-1/100 y; a single settlement's hinterland sees fewer than a region. Band 1/50-1/150; round central value. Per decade per settlement 9.5%. Onset per turn is the exact integration P = 1 - exp(-lambda dt); two uniforms are drawn per settlement per turn UNCONDITIONALLY so lambda = 0 leaves RngStreams bit-identical to lambda > 0 with no strike (the attribution control). Accepted onset-process biases at lambda = 0.01 (CR-015 3.3): no new onset while active plus once-per-turn booking gives ~4.7% of onsets truncated at dt 10 and a ~4.8% rate bias (lambda/(1 + lambda D)) at dt 0.5. durationYears (D): CHOSEN 5.0 inside the historical band 3-7 y (1315-22 Great Famine incl. the murrain, 1601-03, 1695-97, the 1690s seven ill years, 1845-49), at the length the derivation requires; RemainingYears persists BY DIMENSION (a disaster longer than a late-era turn). severityMin/severityMax: fraction of FOOD output lost per ACTIVE year, uniform on [0.75, 1.0] - DERIVED lower edge, historical upper (food output at 0-25% of normal in an active year: Irish potato 1846 ~25% of normal; 1601-03 near-total locally). THE DERIVED BAND: a famine-class event must be able to exhaust the full EFFECTIVE buffer of a settlement at the shipped surplus ratio ALONE at the coarsest era dt: s_min * D > (dt_max (rho_ship - 1) + G) / rho_ship with dt_max = 10, G = 1.5 (consumption.granaryYearsOfDemand) and rho_ship = 1.3 - the DECLARED derivation input (Libur's weather-mean grain surplus ratio in the director's playtest, libur-resources.txt rows 105-116, harvest/eaten 1.03-1.49; the world grain mean ~2.1 is inflated by sparse settlements that overproduce and spoil). Threshold 3.46 production-years; D = 5, s_min = 0.75 gives s*D in [3.75, 5.0]. Dimensional, not a corridor fit: no outcome is targeted, rho_ship enters only as the size of the buffer the event must beat. The turn multiplier is 1 - severity * min(remaining, dt) / dt (dt-exact: a 5-year failure costs 5 s years of food at dt 10 and at dt 0.5 alike); at s_max = 1 it stays >= 0, above 1 it would hand Ledger.Flow a negative source under Throw - the loader refuses s_max > 1, min > max, negative lambda, D <= 0. Where the band sits relative to the weather: a 0.25 yearly multiplier is z = -4.57 under the shipped yearly lognormal (once per ~400,000 settlement-years), so at the year scale the band begins beyond the weather's practical reach; at the decade scale the cause row, not the magnitude, distinguishes them (CR-015 G1, G8).

roads._doc: ADR-032 (transport / inter-city road foundation). EVERY NUMBER IS TUNE — a deterministic PLACEHOLDER (Director rulings 12/14: no cost or speed calibration is ratified). baselineKmPerDay 40: freight speed over the free DirtPath baseline on ideal ground; with the DirtPath capacity below it reproduces the Director's reference figure (5000 t over 3000 km on bad roads ~ 3 in-game months: 3000/40 = 75 days in transit + 5000 t / (100000 t/yr) = 18 days of throughput = 93 days). maxRouteKm 600: the longest straight-line geographic distance (km, settlement site cell to site cell; ADR-032 final ruling 3) between two settlements treated as an inter-city route; a route's LengthKm is that geographic distance, independent of network performance. classes: speedFactor = the class's travel cost per km as a fraction of the baseline's (lower = faster); capacityTonnesPerYear = freight throughput of ONE edge; materialsPerKm = goods.json units consumed per km to build the class from nothing; modernizing a route in place from class X pays only the per-good difference, times the fraction of the modernization performed (a partial modernization pays proportionally). speedFactor must strictly decrease up the ladder (validated): a route part-way between two classes travels at the interpolated SPEED (1/speedFactor), the one value pathfinding, catchments and freight estimates all read. DirtPath is the free baseline and costs nothing. Scale check on the founded seed-42 dev world: settlements hold ~200-700 timber and single-digit stone, pairs are ~100-210 km apart, so a first trackway is affordable and engineered roads wait for an extraction economy — a placeholder, explicitly left for tuning. entity = the research.json infrastructure entity whose knowledge-eligibility makes the class buildable.

governance._doc: ADR-033 D4 (the M5 governing loop, ported from m5-full-build; every number TUNE). authorityDecayCostUnits: DERIVED BY REFERENCE CLASS 25.0 - the e-fold of ADMINISTRATIVE REACH in SettlementDistances travel-cost units, reach = exp(-travelCost / this) from the capital, denominated identically to migration.dampingDecayCostUnits (25.0) with the identical functional form: both answer 'how far does influence travel over this network', so a second unrelated distance scale would assert a magnitude nobody measured (D-040 C3: a distance term over the NETWORK GRAPH, travel cost not Euclidean). SettlementDistances are the authoritative Pathfinder's road-aware costs, so a road that cuts travel cost raises reach (D-040 C6). GovernanceSystem stores the reach in ControlRow.Strength - the ONE stored reach every consumer reads. taxExtractionResponseMax: CHOSEN WITHIN A MEASURED FRAME 0.3 - output multiplier = 1 + this x effectiveRate (effective = declared rate x Strength), framed by production.toolYieldBonusMax (0.3), the tree's statement of how much a multiplier may add to realised production: full extraction is worth at most what fully equipping the settlement with tools is worth. Not derived from a historical series (none exists for this quantity). 0.0 disables the economic arm. taxationRequires: THE RESEARCH GATE of the tax edict (SetTaxRate), one requires-expression over research.json node ids (research dialect: AND / OR / nested, no NOT), validated against research.json at load and evaluated by the existing knowledge evaluator - R5 (Director 2026-10-04: 'taxation is supposed to be a researchable node'): the single dedicated Civics node 'taxation' (key 1007, A3). The four technologies whose capabilities name a taxation refinement - arithmetic_babylonian, surveying, standard_weights, coinage_electrum - keep that text but no longer gate the edict. The tax is a POLICY on flows: no treasury, no receipt, no stock (CR-008).
governance._docTaxationMinAge: H2 (Director 2026-10-05, M5 hardening section 7: 'Taxation is an A3/Bronze Age capability ... taxation must NOT become usable in A1 or A2 merely because the research graph can reach it'; RATIFIED in docs/d049-taxation-and-revolt-model.md). THE AGE HALF OF THE TAX GATE: the tax edict is OPERATIONAL only for a polity whose CURRENT Age (AgeQuery.CurrentAge - computed state, law 4, never a date) is at least this ages.json key. Research is not Age-gated: a polity may complete the Taxation civic in A2 and holds the knowledge, but cannot levy until it enters this Age. Evaluated INSIDE Governance.CanLevyTax together with taxationRequires, so GovernanceSystem (order application on PREV), the AI valve, the available-actions query / UI and every hand-built order meet the one predicate. Absent = no Age requirement (the pre-H2 gate).

ai._doc: ADR-033 D4: the AI tax valve (D-021 valve 6, 'the state acts by default'), the four constants m5-full-build's AiGovernance carried as code literals. An AI Empire that can levy a tax RAISES its declared rate by stepPercent while its legitimacy (population-weighted happiness of what it controls, 0..100) is >= comfortableLegitimacy, LOWERS it while legitimacy is < troubledLegitimacy, holds in the dead band between (the hysteresis that stops a one-step oscillation), and never declares more than maxRatePercent. CHOSEN (M5B's values): the comfortable bar above the 50 midpoint, the troubled bar well below it, a 5-point step (governments adjust, they do not reinvent), and a 40 % ceiling so the AI never taxes itself into revolt on purpose. The player is never touched by this valve.

institutions._doc: ADR-033 D6 (docs/institutions-universities.md): universities as real institutions on ADR-028's lifecycle. EVERY NUMBER IS TUNE; each reference class was fixed BEFORE measuring its effect (CR-003 5.1). Historical figures are approximate (INFERRED from standard histories). Other institution types follow the same lifecycle later (out of scope).

universities._doc: maturityTauYears 16: DERIVED - median founding-to-recognition interval of six early studia (Bologna c.1088->1158 70y, Paris c.1150->1200 ~48, Oxford c.1167->1214 47, Cambridge 1209->1231 22, Montpellier c.1137->1220 83, Salamanca 1218->1243 25; median 47.5) read as the time to the MATURE reading 1-e^-3, so tau = 47.5/3; viable maturation M' = 1-(1-M)exp(-dt/tau). decayTauYears 21.7: DERIVED - an institution that cannot recruit loses its masters at the rate working adults leave the population: 1 / mean(demographics.mortalityPerYear cohorts 3..11 = 0.415/9 = 0.0461/yr); non-viable decay M' = M exp(-dt/tau). matureAt 0.95: 1-e^-3, the three-e-fold convention for 'at its asymptote'. staffShareAtMaturity 0.05: DERIVED - scholars as a share of the host town c.1300 (Paris 1.8%, Padua 2.7%, Montpellier 2.5%, Toulouse 2.9%, Bologna 4.5%, Cambridge 20%, Oxford 23%; median 2.9% of inhabitants / the founded world's adult share 0.563 = ~5% of adults); read as the scholar share of a host at its university market's capacity: each instance employs this x adultsPerUniversity x maturity adults (100 at maturity), so a host keeps at least 95% of its adults in labour while the market term holds; withdrawn from every sector pool (InstitutionStaffing.LabourAdults). Staff proportional to HOST size was measured and rejected: it compounds with the per-instance market (staff share = this x adults / adultsPerUniversity) and withdrew 14-48% of adults in the AI's university hosts at turn 1000 of the seed-42 aiEmpires=1 run. adultsPerUniversity 2000: DERIVED - the smallest high-medieval university town (Cambridge c.1300 ~3,500 inhabitants) x the adult share 0.563 = 1,970; the market each instance needs (adults >= this x (hosted+1) to found, x hosted to sustain) - a per-instance threshold scaled by population, never a maximum count (ADR-028 1.4/2.3). foundingFoodSurplusRatio 1.3 / sustainingFoodSurplusRatio 1.1: IDENTITY - the Artisans emerge/recede thresholds of registries.classes ('the food exists to feed a non-farmer'); scholars are non-food specialists. maxResearchCostReduction 1/3: DERIVED - the ratified calibration's one stated assumption for future research modifiers, x1.5 throughput for a research-optimized civilization (D-045 Part D 3), read as the ceiling of one specialty's discount on its own branch: factor = 1 - this x (1 - e^-X), X the maturity-weighted count of the owner's universities of the type. saturatedAt 0.95: the SATURATED reading of S(X) = 1-e^-X (X >= ~3: the next university adds < 5% of what the first did). healthType: the research.json universityTypes id whose maturity heals. maxMortalityReduction 0.10: DERIVED - smallpox, ~10% of all deaths in 18th-century Europe, is the largest single cause a pre-modern medical establishment removed (variolation, vaccination); multiplier on BASE mortality = 1 - this x (1 - e^-coverage). healthDecayCostUnits 25.0: IDENTITY with migration.dampingDecayCostUnits and governance.authorityDecayCostUnits ('how far does influence travel over this network'); coverage = sum of medical maturities x exp(-SettlementDistances travel cost / this).

colonization._doc: ADR-036 (D-051 section 5, the player/AI Found Settlement order; PROPOSED - the legality terms await the Director's confirmation). orderPartyFraction 0.2: CHOSEN, TUNE. The party a Found Settlement order sends is this fraction of the SOURCE settlement's population, floored to whole people and allocated per bucket by a proportional floor whose remainder goes to the lowest bucket rows first (FoundingQuery.AllocateParty), never emptying a non-empty bucket (the source keeps at least one person in each). The fixed five-field order record carries the source and the site, so the size cannot ride the order. Reference class: D-051 section 5 names Civilization VI settlers as the style - a settler costs one population point and is first affordable in early cities of roughly 3-6 points (INFERRED from play, not measured), i.e. one sixth to one third of the city; 0.2 is one fifth, inside that band. At the turn-zero founding size (founding.cohortCounts, 400 people) it sends 80. The colonists carry provisions = floor(source grain x party / source population) (the existing B1 per-capita share, no new constant), so food per head at the new settlement equals the source's. Read ONLY by the order path: emergent D-037 B1 founding sizes its party from migration's unplaced demand and never reads this (T4.4 section 8 forbids any B1 TUNE). Absent section = no order can form a party (the order is inert).

aiFounding._doc: M5 S1c (ADR-036 section 8; the AI uses the SAME Found Settlement order and the SAME FoundingQuery predicate as the player, D-051 section 5). No ratified AI expansion policy exists (docs/m5-ai-constitution.md is a planning document), so this is the smallest conservative rule, flagged for the Director. Every number TUNE, reference classes fixed BEFORE measuring. enabled true: THE SWITCH - false makes the policy issue nothing, which reproduces every pre-S1c world byte for byte (AiFoundingAttributionTests). minSourcePopulation 500: DERIVED, not tuned - the turn-zero founding size (founding.cohortCounts, 400 people) divided by (1 - orderPartyFraction 0.2), so an AI source still holds at least a newly founded settlement's population after its party of a fifth has left; it also sits at the scale at which archaeology and ethnography commonly report village fission (a few hundred people; INFERRED reference class, not measured here). minYearsBetweenFoundings 350: at most one new settlement per AI polity in 350 years. A settlement here is a regional centre (95.2 km spacing, a 50 km catchment), not a village, and no ratified AI expansion pace exists, so the anchor is the Age ladder's own expansion milestones - a4_expansion asks 14 settlements under one rule, a6_towns 18 - which a polity holding 6 of the canonical 12 at founding (aiEmpires 1) reaches at this pace by about the historical Iron Age (8 foundings in the 2,800 years from the 4000 BCE epoch to ~1200 BCE): the content's pace, not faster (INFERRED anchor). A first value of 50 years (two human generations, the village-fission cadence) was MEASURED on seed 42 and rejected as not conservative: the interval bound at every opportunity, 73 AI foundings in 600 turns, 84 settlements, a 7.8x slower run. It is a DURATION IN YEARS (law 3), measured as a LOWER bound: (turns since the polity's newest settlement was founded) x (the current turn length) - the era table only ever shortens turns, so the gate never opens early and may open a turn late across an era boundary. The other trigger arms read existing state with no new constant: the source is fed (FoodState Normal or Stress - nobody starving), the FoundingQuery people and food arms hold on the source, and an admissible site exists; sites are ranked by the unjittered siting score (SettlementSiting.CandidateScores) with the composite key (score DESC, cell ASC) over the cells FoundingQuery admits. KNOWN LEAK: the AI reads the whole map (no known extent exists until the fog packets), recorded in ADR-036 section 8.

construction._doc: D-051 section 6 applied to construction. AUTHORITY: D-051 section 6 and D-053 section 1 (the Director's 2026-10-13 instruction, item 1: construction and roads draw on the empire stockpile - a settlement must be able to use eligible resources held by other settlements in the same empire; M5 playtest: Bigen waited 62 turns and Shuze 180 for 20 stone while the empire held 128-384; D-053 section 5 records that this instruction supersedes D-052 section 11's deferral for construction and roads). empireStockpile: THE SWITCH, IDENTITY (a rule, not a magnitude - no number is tuned here). true: a construction project in a settlement an Empire controls is checked against, and paid from, the goods of EVERY settlement that Empire controls (one purse, D-051 section 6: instant, lossless, no transport, no wastage); a settlement no Empire controls, and every settlement of a world with no control rows, is its own single-settlement stockpile. DONOR ORDER (Sim.Core/State/EmpireStockpile.cs): the building settlement first, then the Empire's other settlements nearest-first by exact integer squared pixel distance between site cells, ties to the lower settlement id - ADR-032's road payment order with both route ends at the builder; each donor gives min(remaining, held) through the Ledger before the next is touched. COMPETING PROJECTS (incremental off): heads are tried in ascending id, each against what earlier heads left; a lower-id head that passes its gates draws first (a lower-id head that fails a gate - labour, materials, viability - draws nothing and blocks no higher-id head); road development runs later in the same step against what construction left, so no unit is spent twice. With incremental on, the building order is oldest order first (below). CLAIMS: the obtainability guard (a crafted input with no production path, D-051 section 4) reads the purse UNCLAIMED - less the REMAINING inputs (what has not yet gone in) of every project already queued in the Empire's settlements, and of every order accepted earlier in the same batch - so ten tools held once admit one workshop, not one per settlement; and the AI orders a project only when the purse, after counting every queued project's remaining needs and every project it chose earlier in the same decision, covers its whole cost. Claims are counts the guard, the AI and the display read; they set nothing aside themselves - a queue HEAD's set-aside is the reservations rule below (D-055), and a non-head entry's remaining need stays a claim only. Unchanged by empireStockpile: the construction labour is still the building settlement's own, roads already drew on the civilization's purse (ADR-032) and are not switched by this, and storage (the granary bound, spoilage) is untouched. false or absent: the settlement's own stock only, bit-exact - the pre-change rule, which exists ONLY as the golden-attribution control (TestConfigs.PreEmpireConstructionStockpile) - never a gameplay setting. incremental: THE WS1 SWITCH, IDENTITY (a rule, not a magnitude). AUTHORITY: D-054 (the Director's 2026-10-14 instruction, workstream 1: replace the whole-building rule with incremental construction), superseding M4-D's 'built whole or waits'. true: a queue head progresses a little each turn - progress is an integer p of N = 1,000,000 units; each turn it advances by the building settlement's construction labour (capacity C adult-years over the project's laborRequired L, so about C/L of the project a turn) as far as the NEXT units of EVERY material allow: after progress p exactly ceil(cost x p / N) of each input has been delivered, materials first, so nothing advances without the next unit of every input and a shortage of one material never loses what has already gone in. Delivered materials leave the purse through the Ledger as the work goes in (ConstructionMaterials) and are sunk into the project. Labour is a pace, not a gate: a project needing more labour than one turn's capacity simply takes more turns, so no project is unbuildable at a short turn length. BUILDING ORDER: heads are served oldest order first (the turn the order was accepted, then settlement id, then slot), each against what earlier heads left (within the Empire's building share when the split applies, below); road works run later in the step against what building work left. CANCELLING (order kind 13, CancelConstructionEntry, which names the entry by slot, project and order turn - D-056; the legacy slot-only kind 11 is no longer written) loses what has gone in - no refund. The head waits, keeping its progress, while materials are short, there are no builders, an institution's host cannot sustain it, a crafted input cannot be made, or its project left the content. false or absent: the M4-D gate exactly as in batch 2 (the whole cost in the purse and the whole labour this turn, or the head waits) - the golden-attribution control (TestConfigs.PreIncrementalConstruction) only, never a gameplay setting. allocationRatios: THE WS2 SWITCH, IDENTITY (a rule, not a magnitude). AUTHORITY: D-054 (the Director's 2026-10-14 instruction, workstream 2: player-controlled resource-allocation ratios for buildings and roads; do not leave the fixed buildings-first policy silently overriding player settings). true: each Empire has a standing building share b in 0..100 (whole numbers; order kind 12, SetResourceAllocation; no row = 100, 'building first': road works get only what building work leaves - the batch-2 behaviour, and what every AI Empire keeps, since the AI never sets it). ELIGIBLE USES: the two that draw the Empire purse by ORDER - building projects (the construction queue) and road works (DevelopRoads). Dwellings are excluded: housing is needs-driven upkeep drawn from the settlement's own timber before either, never ordered and not purse-based. THE RULE, per Empire, per good g used by either (from goods.json projects and roads.classes, never a code list), when building work starts (after production, trade and housing): S = what the Empire's settlements hold; D_b = what its queue heads would put in this turn with no split (builders and the materials-first lockstep, oldest order first) and, with reservations on, what they set aside (D-055: building work's claim, draws plus set-asides); D_r = what its road order delivered THIS turn would be charged against S (RoadDevelopmentQuery.SimulateCharges - the road system's own arithmetic, so a road order that can pay nothing withholds nothing); building's guaranteed share E_b = floor(S x b / 100) computed exactly, road works' E_r = S - E_b; building work may take G_b = min(D_b, E_b + max(0, E_r - D_r)) - the road share it does not need flows to buildings - and road works then draw from what physically remains, so building share building work did not use flows to roads. Road works can therefore always draw at least min(D_r, E_r) of each good. With no road order delivered, D_r = 0 and building work may use everything; with b = 100 the rule is skipped (G_b = min(D_b, S) never binds). The percentages are guaranteed SHARES of supply against actual demand, never amounts consumed regardless of demand: nothing is spent that a use does not need, nothing is drawn twice (each unit leaves through one Ledger flow), no stock goes negative. Both uses still sink under ConstructionMaterials, so the books do not separate them. The LOADER REFUSES allocationRatios true unless incremental and empireStockpile are both true (a whole-or-wait head capped below its cost could never build; the split is an Empire purse's). false or absent: building work first, road works get what it leaves, exactly as with incremental alone - the golden-attribution control (TestConfigs.PreAllocationRatios) only, never a gameplay setting. reservations: THE D-055 SWITCH, IDENTITY (a rule, not a magnitude). AUTHORITY: D-055 (the Director's batch-4 instruction, item 1: projects must not consume resources reserved by other projects; an older, partially built project must not lose the materials it still needs to a younger one while it cannot advance - this resolves D-054 Q17). true: every construction queue HEAD (the lowest slot of a settlement's queue), at any progress including 0, that is not RELEASED sets aside ('holds') what it still needs, per PURSE and good, in the building order (the turn the order was stamped, then settlement id, then slot - integer keys, total; an entry migrated from schema v32 reads -1 and comes first). THE PURSE KEY is the holder set the head draws from: the controlling Empire's polity id with empireStockpile on and the settlement controlled, otherwise the settlement's own stock (key -1 - settlement id). THE WALK, per purse and good: the budget starts at what the purse holds when building work starts (after production, trade and housing and this step's cancels and enqueues), or at building work's grant G_b under a split; each head in order is resolved against the budget (a head that cannot advance draws 0), the budget falls by its draw, then the head holds min(its remaining need of the good after that draw, what the budget has left) and the budget falls by that hold - the draw first, so draws plus holds never exceed the budget and no hold names a unit that is not there; the oldest unreleased head of a purse is resolved against the whole budget, so a hold never blocks it and holds cannot form a cycle. RELEASED (the reservation is invalid: the holder can never progress in any future state): its project left the content; its settlement has no labour adults (a destroyed or abandoned settlement is a depopulated one); or it founds an institution and no institutions configuration exists. Valid but possibly long waits KEEP holding - materials short, no builders (the player's labour split), a market viability failure, an unobtainable crafted input - and the player sees the holder, the reason and the remedy (give Building a share, or cancel); the AI cancels its own structural stalls as before and never reads the set-asides. RELEASE AND REALLOCATION, exactly: holds are recomputed from scratch every step (no stale state); a cancel (order kind 13) releases in its delivery step and later heads use the units in that step, with no refund; a completion leaves nothing to hold after its final draw and later heads use the leftover in the same step, while the slot it promotes holds from the next step (a cancel's promoted slot holds in the same step); a re-enqueue is a new entry stamped that turn at progress 0, holding only once it is a head, behind every older head; a change of controller moves the hold to the new controller's purse from the next step. Holds bind exactly two things - later construction heads, and road works, which may use only what building work neither drew nor set aside (a single-settlement purse's units are also kept at their own settlement) - and they move no goods: production, consumption, trade, housing and every other consumer are not bound, and the next step recomputes from what exists. Under a split the holds spend building work's grant, so road works still find at least min(D_r, E_r); a head's need beyond the grant is not held. The set-asides are published in the ConstructionHolds table (save schema v34) for road works and the display; construction clears that table at the start of every step whatever this switch says, and road development's read of it is a declared same-step edge (D-056): with this switch on the executor refuses any pipeline that runs road development before construction, so the table is never an input carried from one step to the next (the shipped order, construction before roaddevelopment, is pinned by ConstructionHoldsSchemaV34Tests.TheShippedPipeline_RunsConstructionBeforeRoadDevelopment); with this switch false road development ignores it in any order. The LOADER REFUSES reservations true unless incremental is true (a hold is the remaining need of a part-built head; the whole-or-wait rule has none). empireStockpile is not required: a head's purse is the holder set it draws from, so with the Empire purse off every purse is a single settlement's. false or absent: nothing is set aside and nothing is published - the batch-3 rule exactly - the golden-attribution control (TestConfigs.PreReservations) only, never a gameplay setting. continueWithinTurn: THE D-058 SWITCH, IDENTITY (a rule, not a magnitude). AUTHORITY: D-058 (the Director's ruling of 2026-10-19: 'Build one at a time, so that if 6 can be built and an order of 9 is given, and in that turn, resources are available for 1 more and then some, it should show in the next turn as 7 built, 1 under construction, 1 not started'). true: construction stays SEQUENTIAL - one project of a settlement's queue at a time, in queue order - but one turn's building capacity is not capped at one project: when the head completes, what is left of the settlement's construction capacity that turn (capacity less the adult-years the completed work used) continues to the next entry of the same queue in the same turn, and so on until the capacity or the materials run out; the entry that gets some but not all is part-built, later entries are not started. The continuing entry is resolved at its OWN order's place in the building order (the turn its order was stamped, then settlement id, then slot) against what every older head drew and set aside, exactly as any head - it may spend only what a head in that place may spend, and as a head it sets aside its remaining need in that same turn (this supersedes, for completions, the reservations rule's 'the slot it promotes holds from the next step' above). A project that founds an institution is never started as a continuation: it becomes the head the next turn, when its host's viability is read again. The construction labour published for the settlement is the sum of what its entries used. false or absent: the promoted entry is a head from the next turn and the leftover capacity of the completing turn goes only to dirt paths - the batch-4 rule exactly - the golden-attribution control (TestConfigs.PreContinueWithinTurn) only, never a gameplay setting. The LOADER REFUSES continueWithinTurn true unless incremental is true.

granaries._doc: M5 item 5 - D-053 §3 (the Director, 2026-10-13, item 5: make granaries mechanically meaningful with two distinct effects, a local farm-production bonus and an empire-wide reduction of famine intensity; do not claim granaries increase storage). Two bounded, saturating effects of the BUILT granary (the Structures of the goods.json project named by project; queued granaries count for nothing), each on the ADR-028 curve S(x) = 1 - e^-x that institutions.universities and needs.json taxServiceOffsetMax already use: the first granary adds most and the ceiling is never exceeded. NEITHER EFFECT IS STORAGE: the store bound (consumption.granaryYearsOfDemand) and its spoilage (consumption.grainSpoilagePerYear) are unchanged and ConsumptionSystem never reads this section; the famine-class disaster (disaster.hazardPerYear) is unchanged. The agronomic and historical figures are approximate and INFERRED from standard compilations, not measured here. enabled true: THE SWITCH - false (or the section absent) makes both factors the literal 1.0 and skips both multiplications, which reproduces the pre-granary world byte for byte; it exists as the attribution control (TestConfigs.PreGranaryEffects, GranaryAttributionTests), never a gameplay setting. project 'granary': IDENTITY - the goods.json project whose built count drives both effects (named in data, never a code literal; the ages.json a2_granary fact names it the same way); ProductionSystem and DemographicsSystem resolve it once, at construction. LOCAL FARM OUTPUT: ProductionSystem.Farm multiplies the settlement's REALISED grain rate (after the Leontief minimum, beside weather and extraction, once) by 1 + farmYieldBonusMax x (1 - e^(-m / farmYieldScale)), m = the granaries standing AT that settlement - a granary in A raises A's harvest and no other settlement's. CULTIVATED GRAIN ONLY: while the settlement still harvests WILD FOOD at the forager rates (farming.preCultivation; LabourActivities.HarvestsWildFood, the same predicate that selects those rates) the factor is the literal 1.0 and is not applied - the Director's words are a farm-production bonus, and gathering is not the threshed crop a store protects. MECHANISM: post-harvest loss of the settlement's own crop between the threshing floor and the store, part of which a dedicated dry, raised, sealed store saves. farmYieldBonusMax 0.05: TUNE, bounded by the model's OWN loss accounting. ADR-013's derivation of the cultivated yield (docs/adr/adr-013-lattice-denomination-and-agronomic-recalibration.md, the chain table) already deducts 'x 0.90 storage, vermin and threshing loss' (650 -> 585 kg edible per sown ha) INSIDE the derived 26.0 (farming.yieldPerArableKm2PerYear), so a granary can only recover part of that in-chain 10%, and never the threshing share, which no store saves. Read as about half storage and vermin and half threshing (INFERRED), the ceiling is half of the 10% term, rounded down to 0.05: at the ceiling the retained share becomes 0.90 x 1.05 = 0.945 (585 -> 614 kg per sown ha against 650 before loss), i.e. a saturated granary recovers 45% of the in-chain loss and the remaining 5.5% - all of the threshing share - stays lost; the factor can never restore the pre-loss crop (that would need 1/0.90 = 1.111). For scale only: cereal post-harvest losses in traditional smallholder systems are of the order of 10-15% of the crop (INFERRED from FAO, Global Food Losses and Food Waste, 2011, and APHLIS), consistent with ADR-013's term. NOT DOUBLE-COUNTED WITH SPOILAGE: consumption.grainSpoilagePerYear (0.08) decays the CLOSING STORE carried from year to year (ConsumptionSystem.BoundStore, a Ledger sink on the stock); this factor acts on the NEW crop's loss between the threshing floor and the store, before it is ever stock. The spoilage sink applies unchanged to whatever store exists, including grain a granary saved, and this factor never touches the store. farmYieldScale 1.0: IDENTITY with the project's saturating-count convention (one e-fold per structure - needs.json taxServiceOffsetMax counts public works the same way): one granary +3.2%, two +4.3%, three +4.8% (the 0.95 saturatedAt reading), five +5.0% to the displayed precision and still below the ceiling; each further granary adds strictly less below about the 35th in one settlement (measured in double precision; beyond it the increments are rounding noise, a few 1e-16) and the ceiling +5% is reached in double precision from the 35th - never exceeded. EMPIRE-WIDE FAMINE INTENSITY: DemographicsSystem multiplies the EFFECTIVE deficit (FoodState.EffectiveDeficit - the one input of starvation mortality and of fertility suppression, CR-015 G3(b)) by 1 - famineReductionMax x (1 - e^(-n / famineReductionScale)), n = the granaries standing anywhere in the settlement's civilization (every settlement its controller commands; a stateless settlement counts only its own). The nominal deficit, the FoodState classification, famine flight, happiness and the rebound release gate are unchanged; the factor acts in SEVERE and in FAMINE alike (in NORMAL and STRESS the effective deficit is already 0 and nothing is multiplied). The percentage applies to that SHORTFALL, not to lost births: fertility suppression max(0, 1 - famineFertilitySuppressionSlope x dEff) is already total at dEff >= 1/3, so where the eased shortfall stays at or above that depth births stay halted while starvation eases. NO GRAIN MOVES: the coefficient stands for the civilization's ORGANISED RELIEF CAPACITY - the administration that monitors, rations and directs relief in a shortage, the ever-normal granary system as an institution (Chinese changping cang; the Qing state granaries, P.-E. Will and R. Bin Wong, Nourish the People, 1991; INFERRED) - NOT for stored grain: no stock is credited, debited or transferred by it, so it makes no storage claim. famineReductionMax 0.25: TUNE, CHOSEN - no derivation exists. Reference frame: such reserves held a small fraction of annual consumption (INFERRED: of the order of 5% at the 18th-century peak) and could not replace a lost harvest; they blunted and shortened the crisis where relief was organised. A quarter of the unabsorbed intensity is the conservative ceiling: a civilization saturated with granaries still starves at three quarters of the ungranaried rate, and the factor stays in [0.75, 1], so the effective deficit is never inverted and never raised. famineReductionScale 2.0: TUNE, CHOSEN with a stated rationale, not derived: one granary per settlement of a polity of about 6 settlements (the AI polity of the canonical 12-settlement world, aiEmpires 1, as colonization.aiFounding._doc reads it; the Qing design target of one public granary per county seat is the historical frame, INFERRED) reaches the SATURATED reading 1 - e^-3 = 0.95 (institutions.universities.saturatedAt): scale = 6 / 3. n is an ABSOLUTE count, not per settlement or per head: one granary relieves a one-settlement and a sixty-settlement civilization alike (-9.8% in both), and six reach the 0.95 reading in either - stated, not normalised (a size-normalised count would be a new design). One granary in the civilization -9.8%, two -15.8%, five -22.9%, six -23.8%, fifty -25.0% to the displayed precision and still strictly above the 0.75 floor; each further granary reduces strictly less below about the 69th (measured in double precision; beyond it the increments are rounding noise) and the floor is reached in double precision only from the 72nd - never passed. Loader: project names a goods.json project; both maxima in [0, 1); both scales finite and > 0.

discovery._doc: M6 Track EX (D-062, ADR-044): concealed ore deposits and the Prospect order (OrderKind 15). enabled true: THE SWITCH - false (or the section absent) conceals nothing and refuses Prospect, which reproduces the pre-M6 world byte for byte after the v35 sections are stripped (the attribution control TestConfigs.PreDiscovery). concealableGoods: IDENTITY (coordinator ruling under D-062) - only the ORES (copper-ore, tin-ore) can be hidden; stone and clay are surface quarry goods and, like livestock, fish, timber, fiber and hides, are never concealed. concealedShare 0.25: DIRECTOR (D-062) - of a settlement's n eligible deposit rows (abundance > 0, a concealable good), k = floor(n x 0.25 + u) are concealed, u = frac(h(seed) + 0.6180339887498949 x settlementId) a low-discrepancy offset (h a stateless SplitMix64 hash of the seed), so the realized share stays near 0.25 even with n <= 2; the rows chosen are the k lowest by (hash(seed, settlement, good), goodId); no RNG stream is drawn and the deposit table is unchanged. A concealed row reads as abundance 0 for the settlement's controller until that polity prospects the settlement. prospectGrain 40: TUNE, MEASURED (ADR-044 section 5) - the survey party's provisions, sunk under reason Prospecting through EmpireStockpile.Draw like Explore's; under a tenth of a typical settlement's grain store from turn 5 on (seeds 1, 2, 42, 7), so a settlement can prospect within the first few dozen turns without risking its food. prospectDiscountRequires copper_smelting: the ore-recognition technology (recognising malachite and azurite as ore is the knowledge copper smelting embodies) - with it completed the cost halves (integer division).

fog._doc: M6 Track EX (D-062, ADR-044): the minimal fog of war and the Explore order (OrderKind 14). enabled true: THE SWITCH - false (or absent) makes PolityKnowledge.Of answer all-known exactly as before and DiscoverySystem write nothing (the attribution control TestConfigs.PreDiscovery). Distances are traversal-lattice nodes of 16 km. seedRadiusNodes 3 (about 50 km): the model's own hinterland constant (catchment.hinterlandRadiusKm 50) - every step each polity knows the disc of this radius around every settlement it controls. formationSightNodes 1: a formation sees its own node and its 8-neighbourhood disc of radius 1. exploreStepNodes 3: one Explore widens a settlement's explored radius by one hinterland; exploreMaxRadiusNodes 15 (about 240 km) caps it - beyond that is M7's mobile scouting. exploreGrain 60: TUNE, MEASURED (ADR-044 section 5) - the expedition's travel provisions, sunk under reason Expedition (people are not removed; the M7 mobile unit replaces this).
